speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song
text: asked the Minister for Transport in the last three years (a) how many applications for the (i) Taxi Driver's Vocational Licence (ii) Private Hire Car Driver's Vocational Licence (iii) Bus Driver's Vocational Licence (iv) Bus Attendant's Vocational Licence and (v) Omnibus Driver's Vocational Licence were rejected due to the criminal record of the applicants for offences other than rape, murder or kidnapping respectively; and (b) of these, how many appeals were received and how many were approved upon appeal.

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
text: I understand that those who have committed offences like rape, murder and kidnapping will not get a licence.

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
text: And I think that is a reasonable safeguard for passengers.

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
text: However, I have met residents who told me they cannot get back their VL for past convictions for less violent or non-violent offences.

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
text: This prevents them from earning a living and re-integrating into society.

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
text: So, can the Senior Minister of State please provide more clarity on what offences will debar a person from obtaining this licence?

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
text: I think this will also give some clarity to the passengers to know that drivers who have gotten offences in the past will not be a safety threat to themselves.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: As the Member has rightly pointed out, we need to strike a balance, we need to maintain public confidence, especially for passengers conveyed in public service vehicles, like taxis and private hire cars.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: Whilst we want to give the applicant who has had a criminal record before a second chance in taking up driving as a vocation, we also need to ensure that the interest and safety of commuters are safeguarded.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: So, when we look at the applications, the Member has asked whether there are specific offences that we consider.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: Actually, criminal offences make up a large range.
